questions.text: A quality team has completed a PDSA cycle and found that the intervention did not achieve the desired outcome. What is the MOST appropriate next step?

options.a: Abandon the improvement project and select a new priority
options.b: Implement the intervention organization-wide and monitor results
options.c: Analyze what was learned and revise the intervention for the next PDSA cycle
options.d: Report the failure to senior leadership and await direction

questions.explanation: The PDSA cycle is iterative. When an intervention does not work, the team analyzes what was learned and uses that knowledge to revise the approach in the next cycle.

questions.text: Which type of waste in Lean methodology refers to producing more than is needed or producing earlier than needed?
questions.explanation: Overproduction is considered the most critical waste in Lean because it leads to excess inventory and can hide other problems.

questions.text: A hospital wants to reduce the time from ED arrival to physician assessment. Which tool would BEST help map the current state process?
questions.explanation: Value stream mapping visualizes the entire flow of a process, including steps, delays, and handoffs, making it ideal for identifying waste and inefficiencies.

questions.text: In Six Sigma, a process operating at 'Six Sigma quality' produces approximately:
questions.explanation: Six Sigma quality is defined as no more than 3.4 defects per million opportunities, representing near-perfect process performance.

questions.text: Which of the following is the PRIMARY purpose of the 'Control' phase in DMAIC?

options.a: Identifying root causes of the problem
options.c: Sustaining the gains achieved and preventing regression
options.d: Defining the problem scope and goals

questions.explanation: The Control phase focuses on sustaining improvements by implementing monitoring systems, standard procedures, and response plans to prevent regression.

questions.text: A quality professional is tasked with reducing patient wait times in the outpatient clinic. After mapping the process, which activity should be targeted FIRST?

options.a: Steps that add the most value to the patient
options.b: Steps where clinical staff spend the most time
options.c: Steps that do not add value and can be eliminated (waste)

questions.explanation: Lean improvement prioritizes identifying and eliminating non-value-added steps (waste) as the most effective way to reduce wait times.

questions.text: A run chart shows 8 consecutive data points all above the median. This pattern indicates:

options.b: A signal of special cause variation

questions.explanation: Eight or more consecutive data points on the same side of the median is a run chart rule for special cause variation, suggesting a real change in the process.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a 'process measure' in quality improvement?

options.a: A measure of patient health outcomes such as mortality rate
options.b: A measure of whether a specific step in the care process was performed

questions.explanation: Process measures assess whether specific evidence-based care steps were completed, such as whether a patient received a recommended screening.

questions.text: Which framework specifically uses 'tollgates' to review progress at each phase before proceeding?
questions.explanation: DMAIC uses formal tollgate reviews at the end of each phase, where leadership reviews progress and approves moving to the next phase.

questions.text: A hospital implements a new sepsis bundle and tracks compliance monthly. After six months, compliance remains consistently above 95%. This is an example of:

options.a: A process in special cause variation
options.b: A sustained improvement that has become the new standard
options.c: A temporary improvement that requires re-testing

questions.explanation: Consistent performance at the desired level over multiple measurement periods indicates the improvement has been sustained and incorporated into standard practice.
